knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the customer buys a result with a stated time and limit, not an hourly rate. Your van and tool list and years in business are not what the customer buys.
The lesson says a guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford, and that any extra guarantee should be limited to what you control. An open-ended or impossible guarantee does not meet this.
The lesson says extra work needs the customer's permission first, and it should be priced in writing. Doing the task and invoicing later, or adding it without telling the customer, is not acceptable.
